# Coditu

> Coditu builds SharePoint and SPFx web parts and internal apps for small and mid-size
> organisations in Germany, plus the Baukasten — a library of Microsoft 365 building blocks,
> in the client's design, with Microsoft Entra sign-in, hosted on the client's own server. One
> team, with hubs in Berlin and Cairo, owns a project from the first sketch through to ongoing
> operation. Contact: contact@coditu.com.

## What we build

- [SharePoint web parts](https://coditu.com/en#services): Web parts that slot into existing SharePoint pages and show the client's SharePoint lists live. Over 40 built for one organisation; a new web part is usually 5–10 hours of work.
- [SharePoint web parts development](https://coditu.com/en/services/sharepoint-web-parts-development): Dedicated page on getting a SharePoint/SPFx web part redesigned or built — in the client's design, live from their SharePoint lists, usually 1–2 days.
- [SPFx developer](https://coditu.com/en/services/spfx-developer): Dedicated page for SPFx development specifically — one team (no subcontractors), weekly sprints, billed by the hour or per piece.
- [SharePoint development, Berlin](https://coditu.com/en/services/sharepoint-development-berlin): Dedicated page for SharePoint/SPFx development with a fixed contact based in Berlin.
- [SharePoint development, Bavaria](https://coditu.com/en/services/sharepoint-development-bavaria): Dedicated page for companies in Bavaria; projects may qualify for the Digitalbonus.Bayern public funding programme.
- [SharePoint development, North Rhine-Westphalia](https://coditu.com/en/services/sharepoint-development-nrw): Dedicated page for companies in North Rhine-Westphalia, served remotely from Berlin and Cairo.
- [Internal apps](https://coditu.com/en#services): Small, focused apps built from a sketch — requests, onboarding, editorial calendars — signed in with Microsoft and permissioned by group. A first version typically takes 10–14 hours.
- [Websites & web apps](https://coditu.com/en#services): Fast, SEO-structured websites and product pages.
- [The Baukasten](https://coditu.com/en#baukasten): Coditu's own product — React components that snap together, Microsoft Entra sign-in, deployed on the client's own server so data never leaves their system.

## Facts

- Team: Mohamed Tamer (Frontend Lead, Cairo), Adam Nafie (Client Partnerships, Berlin), Abdelrahman Elkhateeb (Frontend Engineer, Cairo), Ahmed Yehia (Backend & DevOps, Cairo). Four people, hubs in Berlin and Cairo.
- One reference project: a SharePoint intranet for an organisation in Germany, in weekly sprints for almost a year — the client stays anonymous.
- Pricing: rates are well below the German market average for SharePoint and SPFx development (that average runs around €95/hour — junior €80–100, senior €120–160). Coditu's exact rates are quoted per project, not published as a flat figure; larger projects get a discount. See https://coditu.com/en/blog/sharepoint-web-part-cost for the full market comparison.
- Data lives in the client's own Microsoft 365 and SharePoint; Microsoft holds it, not Coditu. The client owns the code, the documentation and keeps full control.

## FAQ

- **What does a project cost?** The price depends on the amount of work — rates are well below the German market average for SharePoint/SPFx development. Larger projects get a discount, plus a little extra on top. See the Facts section above for the market comparison.
- **How soon is there a first version?** A new web part usually takes 1–2 days; the first version of an internal app is ready in a few days.
- **Do you only work with SharePoint and Microsoft 365?** No — Coditu also builds internal apps, websites and frontends, and looks after them after launch.
- **What does working together look like?** Weekly sprints: every week shows what's done, the client says what should change, one fixed contact throughout.
- **You're in Berlin and Cairo — how does that work?** The fixed client contact, Adam Nafie, is based in Berlin; Berlin and Cairo are at most one hour apart; conversations happen in German or English.
- **Who owns the code?** The client does — code, documentation and full control, no lock-in.
- **What happens after go-live?** Coditu stays on hand for changes and maintenance, billed per request.
